image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a ground covered with dry leaves and dirt. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, grey/brown body plumage, and orange webbed feet. It is viewed from a high-angle side profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellowish-green hue typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and compact. The plumage appears dense and layered, fitting the description of a waterfowl.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg and foot are clearly visible. The foot shows webbing between the toes, and the leg position is consistent with waterfowl anatomy.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing broad feather structures and a tapered end.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (speculum area nearby also visible) is present.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or misclassified bird types.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs, which are common AI artifacts in birds.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex feather textures and the background leaves, ensuring sharp boundaries.
To assess general texture consistency and look for subtle melting or noise in the feather details.

focus_areas: Feather texture consistency and boundary sharpness against the leafy background
Anatomical correctness of the webbed foot and leg joint
Iridescence rendering on the green head feathers

Also, verify that the 'curl' of the tail feathers is structurally connected to the body and not floating.
